stopCases.issue: The paraphrase says OpenAI describes Version 2 as an update to "its framework first released in 2023", and the locator cites "opening paragraphs describing the first update since the 2023 framework". Neither the live announcement nor its 2025-04-16 capture mentions 2023, Beta or a first release; the Version 2 PDF does not either. The page calls it "an update to our Preparedness Framework" without naming a predecessor.
stopCases.effect: The evidence as written widens what the source says; the claim that Version 2 replaces Beta rests on this one evidence record.
stopCases.disposition: Not resolved. Week 4a: candidate for requalification or additional evidence. Evidence and claim unchanged.

proposerRetrievalFailures.detail: The Internet Archive answered HTTP 429 to scripted requests for about an hour; four archived pages (FSF v2 update, Preparedness v2 announcement, RSP archive, RSP v3 release) were then read through the in-app browser instead.

limits: A bounded sample does not certify unsampled records. PDF text layers can drop word spaces; one quote (evidence-rsp-v3-4-coverage-date) restores two such spaces, as stated in its note. Machine agreement is neither historical certainty nor human review.
